title: Notion Pricing Plans: Free, Plus, Business, & Enterprise.
text:
### Free

$0 per member / month

For individuals to organize personal projects and life.

Includes:

- Trial of Notion AI
- Basic forms
- Basic sites
- Notion Calendar
- Databases including subtasks, dependencies, custom properties and more

### Plus

$10 per member / month

For small teams and professionals to work together.

Everything in Free, and:

- Trial of Notion AI
- Custom forms
- Custom sites
- Charts
- Collaborative blocks
- File uploads
- Basic connections

## The AI workspace for work that matters.

### Business Recommended

$20 per member / month

For growing businesses to streamline teamwork.

Everything in Plus, and:

- Notion Agent
- AI Meeting Notes
- Enterprise Search Beta
- SAML SSO
- Granular database permissions
- Verify any page
- Private teamspaces
- Domain verification
- Premium connections

### Enterprise

Custom pricing

For organizations to operate with scalability, control, and security.

Everything in Business, and:

- Zero data retention with LLM providers
- User provisioning (SCIM)
- Advanced security & controls
- Audit log
- Customer success manager
- Security & Compliance connections (DLP, SIEM)
- Domain management
- Advanced connections

...

How is pricing calculated for the paid plans?

If you upgrade your workspace to one of the paid plans, you will be charged a fee per member.

Guests are free of charge – but they can only access individual pages they are invited to. In other words, guests won’t be able to see all the team pages under the `Teamspaces` section in the left sidebar.

How do I get charged when I add members to my workspace?

When you add a new member to your workspace, they will use an existing paid seat if you have any available in your workspace. If you do not have any existing available paid seats, your count of paid seats will increase by 1. Changes in membership that occur mid-month will create prorated charges based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle when the paid seat was added.

For every member you delete from your workspace, you will open up 1 available paid seat. This means you have the option to exchange members in your workspace without paying any additional costs, as long as your total billable seat count remains the same.

title: Notion Pricing 2026: Plans, AI Cost, Free Trial
text:
Notion costs $0 on Free, $10 per member per month on Plus and $20 on Business when billed yearly (Notion's pricing page, checked October 17, 2026). Solo users and small teams that don't need Notion Agent or SSO should stay on Free or Plus, and Business is the upgrade for teams that want built-in AI, private teamspaces and 90-day history.

...

- On yearly billing, Notion lists Free at $0, Plus at $10 and Business at $20 per member per month; Enterprise is custom-priced (official pricing page, checked 2026-10-17).
- Independent guides put monthly billing at $12 for Plus and $24 for Business. By our calculation, yearly billing then saves about 17% per seat, while Notion's banner says "up to 20%".
- Notion Agent and AI Meeting Notes are included in Business and Enterprise seat prices. Free and Plus get only a limited trial, and the pricing page lists no separate AI add-on.
- Custom Agents are free to try, then cost $10 per 1,000 monthly Notion credits on top of seat prices.
- The standard trial is 30 days of Business, but only for teams on a professional email domain. Gmail-style and school addresses don't qualify.
- The startup program gives 1 to 6 months of Business free. The 3- and 6-month offers are meant for startups building scalable, tech-related products or services, while service businesses and SMBs get 1 month.
- Students and educators can get Plus free for one member with a school email.

...

### Notion (Plus and Business plans)

Best for: Solo users and small teams that want one workspace for notes, docs and wikis, and startups that may qualify for free Business months

Free covers one person well, Plus suits a small team that outgrows the free block limit, and Business is the step for Notion Agent, SSO and private teamspaces. Business costs twice as much as Plus, so upgrade only when you need a Business-only feature.

- Free plan with unlimited pages and blocks for one person
- Guests are free and don't count as paid seats
- 30-day Business trial for eligible teams
- Startup program can cover 1 to 6 months of Business

- Business costs twice as much as Plus
- Removed seats aren't refunded mid-cycle
- Card payments only
- Custom Agents are billed on top of seat prices

Price: From $10 (Plus) or $20 (Business) per member per month billed yearly, checked October 2026. Confirm tax and any monthly pricing at checkout.

## Comparison at a glance

| Team size | Plus, billed yearly | Business, billed yearly | Business premium per year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 seats | $600 | $1,200 | $600 |
| 20 seats | $2,400 | $4,800 | $2,400 |

...

## How much does Notion cost in 2026?

Notion is free to start, but anything beyond personal use is a per-seat subscription. These are the list prices on Notion's official pricing page, checked on October 17, 2026, in the US dollar view and before sales tax:

- Free: $0, aimed at individuals organizing personal projects.
- Plus: $10 per member per month, for small teams and professionals.
- Business: $20 per member per month, the plan Notion marks as recommended.
- Enterprise: custom price, you contact sales.

The $10 and $20 figures are yearly-billing prices. Notion's page has a Pay monthly / Pay yearly toggle and says you can save up to 20% with yearly billing. Independent guides such as Rock and PageDog put monthly billing at $12 for Plus and $24 for Business. By our calculation from those figures, that is about 17% saved per seat on yearly billing.

You pay per member. Guests are free but only see the pages they're invited to. Adding someone mid-cycle creates a prorated charge, while removing someone gives no credit, and seats are recounted at renewal. Payment is by credit or debit card only.

A custom domain is an extra on every plan: $8 per month per domain billed yearly, or $10 billed monthly. If you just want to see the app first, you can open a free Notion workspace and upgrade later.

## What do you get on the Notion Free plan, and when is it not enough?

Free works well for one person. Pages and blocks are unlimited when you're the only member, so notes, tasks and a personal wiki cost nothing.

The limits show up with a team. Once a workspace has 2 or more members, the free plan caps the number of blocks. Notion doesn't publish the exact figure on its pricing page. When you hit the cap, you can still read, edit and organize existing blocks, but you can't add new ones.

The other Free limits, from the official comparison table:

- File uploads: 5 MB per file (paid plans have no cap beyond roughly 5 GB per file)
- Page history: 7 days
- External guests: 10
- Charts: 1
- Automations: buttons only, with no custom database automations

A two-person freelance studio sharing a client wiki will likely hit the block cap first. A solo user storing large PDFs will hit the 5 MB upload limit first. Either is a fair reason to move to Plus.

...

## Notion Plus vs Business: which plan fits your team?

Plus removes the everyday limits: unlimited blocks, guests and charts, 30-day page history and custom database automations. Business adds what matters once several people, clients or security rules are involved.

Beyond Plus, Business includes:

- Notion Agent and AI Meeting Notes
- SAML SSO and domain verification
- private teamspaces and granular database permissions
- verified pages
- premium connections such as GitHub and Asana
- 90-day page history (Plus has 30)

Enterprise goes further with SCIM user provisioning, advanced security controls, an audit log, zero data retention with AI model providers (other plans have 30-day retention) and a customer success manager.

The table below shows yearly cost on yearly billing, excluding sales tax, custom domains and Custom Agent credits. Across 5 seats, Business costs $600 more per year than Plus. Across 20 seats, the gap is $2,400. The real question is whether private teamspaces, SSO or built-in AI are worth that to your team.

Our rule of thumb:

- Solo user: stay on Free until you need larger uploads or longer history, then Plus.
- Small team of 2 to 10 sharing a wiki and projects: Plus, unless you need AI for everyone or restricted spaces.
- Startup with investors, contractors or sensitive data: Business, ideally with the free months below.

...

### The standard 30-day trial

According to Notion's paid plan trials page, eligible teams get 30 days of Business with all its features, including Notion AI, SAML SSO and private teamspaces. You need a professional email domain and no existing Business or Enterprise plan. Personal or educational domains such as Gmail don't qualify, and you must start the trial from the web or desktop app. The page mentions no Plus trial.

If you entered card details, Business renews automatically at the end, even when you started the trial from Plus. To cancel the trial, go to Settings → Explore plans before the 30 days run out. You then drop to Free, or straight back to Plus if you started from Plus.

### The startup program

Notion for Startups offers 1 to 6 months of Business free, including Notion AI, for new, non-paying customers. The 3- and 6-month offers are intended for startups building scalable, tech-related products or services. Service businesses and SMBs get 1 month. The length depends on who you are:

- Partner-affiliated startups with a code from their partner: 6 months
- Non-partner startups: 3 months on a new Business plan
- Small and medium businesses (including service businesses), teams under 10 employees, or applicants Notion can't fully verify: 1 month

The 6-month offer lists a valid Notion domain, a public company website, a company email address and fewer than 100 employees. It only applies to net new Business plans. Notion decides eligibility and says it will reach out within 2 to 5 business days if you're a good fit. So treat "up to 3 months" as a best case for a non-partner tech startup, not a promise. A team under 10 people may get just 1 month.

...

Start with the cheapest plan that removes the limit you actually hit.

- Just you, notes and personal projects: Free. Students and educators should take the free Plus instead.
- You need big uploads, 30-day history or automations: Plus at $10 per seat on yearly billing.
- A team that wants Notion Agent, SSO or private teamspaces: Business at $20 per seat, ideally after the 30-day trial or the startup program.
- Large organization with audit and provisioning needs: talk to Notion sales about Enterprise.

title: Notion vs Obsidian for Solopreneurs: Pick by the Job (2026)
text:
## The short answer

Pick Notion if most of what you track has a status, a due date or a price: content calendars, launch checklists, product lists, a simple sales pipeline. Its databases and its free calendar app do that work, and the Free plan lists unlimited blocks for a single user.

Pick Obsidian if most of what you produce is writing and thinking: research notes, scripts, newsletter drafts, a long-lived idea file.

...

If you do both kinds of work heavily, run both. Give each job one home. That last rule matters more than the choice itself.

...

The Free plan is more usable for one person than its name suggests. As of October 2026 it lists unlimited blocks for a solo user, 10 external guests, basic forms and one chart. The limits show up elsewhere: 5 MB per uploaded file and 7 days of page history. If you store video cuts, design files or big PDFs in your workspace, Free won’t hold them. Plus raises uploads to roughly 5 GB per file and history to 30 days.

Calendar is the second strong argument. Notion Calendar is a free app that syncs Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars, and once your workspace is linked, dated items from a Notion database show up as events. You can also attach or create a Notion page from inside an event. If you already book calls through a scheduler, our guide to scheduling tools for solopreneurs covers that side.

The weak spot is AI pricing. Notion’s own help center says Notion AI is available on Business and Enterprise, while Free and Plus users get a limited number of complimentary responses. If you choose Notion mainly for AI, you’re choosing the $20 tier, not the $10 one.

...

## What one person actually pays, October 2026

Most comparisons list plan prices without saying which ones a solo operator would actually buy. The table below prices the realistic setups for one person, collected from the official pricing and help pages on October 19, 2026.

| Setup for one person | Monthly cost | Billed yearly | The limit you’ll hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notion Free | $0 | $0 | 5 MB per file, 7-day page history, AI trial only |
| Notion Plus | $10 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | Notion AI still trial-only |
| Notion Business (for Notion AI) | $20 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | AI usage allowance is included, but premium models use Notion credits |
| Obsidian, no add-ons | $0 | $0 | You handle sync yourself |
| Obsidian + Sync Standard | $5 | $4/month | 1 GB total, 5 MB per file, 1 synced vault, 1 month of history |
| Obsidian + Sync Plus | $10 | $8/month | 10 GB (upgradable to 100 GB), 200 MB per file, 10 vaults, 12 months of history |
| Add Obsidian Publish | +$10 per site | +$8/month per site | One site per subscription |
| Optional Obsidian commercial license | n/a | $50 per user per year | Not required for business use |

Notion’s pricing page lists Plus at $10 and Business at $20 per member a month and says yearly billing saves up to 20%, but it doesn’t label which billing period the headline figure assumes. Check the toggle at checkout before you commit to a year.

The practical read: a solo writer on Obsidian with Sync Standard pays $48 a year. A solo operator who wants AI inside Notion pays the Business rate. Everything in between depends on whether your notes include large files.

title: Notion vs Obsidian vs Coda for Solo Founders (2026) - The Real AI Operator
text:
- Pick Notion if you want one place for docs, tasks, CRM, and a wiki. It’s cloud-only, and per-seat pricing adds up the second you bring in collaborators. I use it every day, for what that’s worth.
- Pick Obsidian if you write a lot and your notes are how you think. Everything lives on your own machine. No subscription, no lock-in, no third party deciding whether you still have access tomorrow.
- Pick Coda if ops is what’s eating your week. It turns pipelines, trackers, and internal tools into docs you can maintain without paging a developer.

...

## Pricing for a one-person company

What you pay boils down to two things: how many people touch the workspace and which features you actually use. Here’s what a solo founder sees in August 2026.

- Notion: Free for personal use. Plus runs $10 per member per month on annual billing ($12 if you go monthly). Most solo folks stay on Free until they hit the file upload cap or need longer page history.
- Obsidian: The desktop app is free on every platform. If you want your iPad and phone to stay in sync, add Obsidian Sync at $4 a month, billed annually.
- Coda: Free for unlimited viewers. Pro is $10 per Doc Maker per month on annual billing. Most solo founders stick with Free because there’s only one of you editing.

The catch nobody mentions upfront: Notion bills per member, including people who just read. Coda bills per Doc Maker. So if you share your workspace with five advisors who only read, Notion charges you for six seats. Coda charges you for one. I set up a Notion workspace for a client a while back and handed out a few guest logins without thinking too hard about it. The bill at the end of the month made me wince.

Flip the math to a 20-person team and it reverses. Notion’s flat per-seat pricing usually beats Coda’s free-viewer play once everyone’s actively editing. So don’t pick on pricing alone. Look at who’s actually writing in the doc versus who’s just lurking.

...

For a solo founder starting from scratch, no cofounder, no team, just you and the work, I’d start with Notion Free. It’s what I use for my own company wiki, CRM, and task board. Day-one basics for a one-person company, and Notion ships them out of the box.

title: Notion Promo Code: 3 months free Business (July 2026) | SaaSOffers
text:
## 3 Months Free Notion Business: The Offer

Offer: 3 months free Business.

There is no promo code. Apply with a company email and a live website. Business costs $24 per member a month on monthly billing, so a 10-person team saves $720 over the 3 months, and Notion's startup page says the free period includes Notion AI. The Free plan stops at 1,000 blocks once you add a second member and has no full AI. Notion runs a very similar program itself, and it can assign teams under 10 employees 1 month instead.

We checked these plans and prices against Notion's official pricing and help pages in November 2026.

Notion is one workspace for docs, wikis, databases and project tracking, with AI built into the ... Notion, not SaaSOffers, sets the final terms.

## Our Offer Next to Notion's Own Startup Program

Notion runs a public program at notion.com/startups, and anyone can apply directly. All 3 tiers are on Business with monthly AI credits.

| Tier | Who gets it (Notion's wording, shortened) | Free period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Partner | Under 100 employees and affiliated with a select Notion startup partner; needs a code from the partner | 6 months |
| Standard | Under 100 employees, a valid business website, a company domain email | 3 months |
| SMB | Under 10 employees, SMBs and service businesses, or startups Notion could not fully verify | 1 month |

- Same length as Notion's public tier. Our 3 months matches what Notion publishes for non-partner startups. We do not beat it.
- Shorter than the partner tier. If your VC or accelerator is a Notion partner, ask for their code. 6 months beats our 3, and Notion allows only one offer per customer.
- Teams under 10 should check the length. Notion's startup FAQ says companies under 10 employees receive the 1 month trial. Its help page says this typically applies when a company misses its startup criteria or cannot be verified. Our listing says 3 months, and we could not confirm which rule applies, so check the length in Notion's approval email.
- If you get 1 month, that matches the length of Notion's public 30-day Business trial.

Notion's other rules: you must be a new, non-paying customer with a work email (no Gmail or Outlook) and no previous Notion promotion. Offers cover net-new Business plans, not Enterprise, and cannot be combined with other offers or codes.

The 3 and 6 month tiers are for startups building scalable, tech-related products or services. Consultancies, agencies and service businesses get 1 month. So can applicants with a parked website, only personal social profiles, or an application that looks like one person.

## Notion Pricing in November 2026

Prices are per member, per month, in USD. Yearly billing saves $4 per member a month on Business, about 17%.

| Plan | Billed yearly | Billed monthly | Key limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | $0 | 1,000 blocks once a workspace has 2 or more members, 5 MB per file, 7 days of page history, 10 guests, 1 chart, basic forms, limited AI trial |
| Plus | $10 | $12 | No block limit, 5 GB per file, 30 days of page history, custom forms, database automations, limited AI trial |
| Business | $20 | $24 | Notion AI with 1,500 Standard and 500 Select credits per member a month, 90 days of page history, SAML SSO, private teamspaces, granular database permissions, verified pages |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Contact sales | SCIM, audit log, custom page history, zero data retention with LLM providers, advanced security controls, customer success manager |

## When Notion is the wrong pick

- Backed by a Notion partner. Ask your investor for the 6-month code instead.
- Already paying for Notion. The offer is for non-paying customers, and past invoices are not refunded.

- Solo founders on Gmail. A personal address fails the work email rule.
- Teams that need SCIM, audit logs or a HIPAA BAA. Those sit on Enterprise, and the offer does not cover Enterprise.
